speaker: paulmcleish
text: Manningham Council acknowledges the Wurundjeri people as the traditional custodians of the land we now know as Manningham. We pay our respect to Wurundjeri elders past and present and value the ongoing contribution to the cultural heritage of Manningham. Council would also like to acknowledge the contribution made to Manningham over the years by people of diverse backgrounds and cultures. I welcome all members of the public to this council meeting this evening who have joined us online to observe proceedings. In response to the evolving coronavirus situation, changes have been made to the Local Government Act which permit council meetings to be held virtually for a limited time. The health and safety of our community and employees is our priority during these uncertain times. So we will continue to hold our meetings virtually to further reduce the risk of transmission of COVID-19. You will notice a few changes to how we are conducting our meetings. You won't be able to attend our meetings in person. However you are, as you know, we'll be able to watch the meeting live through our website and Facebook page. You can also watch the recording at any time after the meeting when it suits you. Council acknowledges that in the lead up to its general elections, it will not make any decisions that would or could be perceived to inappropriately bind an incoming council or affect the outcome of the elections. As stipulated in our election period policy 2020, council will hold a meeting this month to consider routine administrative matters and the annual report. There are also limitations placed on the conduct of the meeting such as no public question time, tabling of petitions and council question time. Finally, I would like to advise that if we experienced technical issues during the meeting, we will make every attempt to resolve them within 30 minutes. If we are unable to resolve the issue, the meeting will be adjourned to another time and date. A notice will be placed on the council website advising the meeting has been adjourned and when it is expected to reconvene. Council meetings are governed by Manningham's governance rules. I will introduce each item of business as listed on the agenda, calling it by number and by reading the title. I will then call for a mover and seconder of a motion on the item before opening any debate. Only councillors are able to join the debate on an item. Councillors may adopt the officer's recommendation in the report or propose amendments and supplementary motions. Item two, apologies and requests for leave of absence. While I'm fairly certain there are no leaves of absence requests, so I would now just like to confirm the attendance of councillors. Councillor Mike Zafiropoulos. Present. Councillor Anna Chen.

And within a month, we need to actually vote on this and accept this as the true and accurate record of our year. Annual reports are an important part of local government. Indeed, they're an important part of all companies and businesses that deal with the community. It's here and it outlines, I suppose, A, what our company or what MacCouncil is about, and it really describes our area. But it also goes in on our performance and how we've gone over the year. And over the years, they've been refined more and more, and there's a bit of a template. So when you go to any council website now or council AGM, or not AGM, report, annual report, they're similar in nature in set out. And it is there to look and compare and to make a record of what has been done in that past year and what achievements we've achieved and areas that we need to improve on and areas that we've excelled in or whatever. And that's a great document that is there for the record for the future and indeed for recording how we've done. So our annual reports, and we've got the audited statements that are going to join what is on the paper tonight and the forward from the Mayor and CEO, which is part of that.
